$comment: Lane L19. What each option of OpenDesigner's high-impact questions changes. Covers every question with weight high (pacing.json time_weight_rule: a decided card with fan-out 5+ or a Quick question): 30 questions, which include every question named in pacing.json top_decisions and Q-motion-01. Per option: 'now' = what changes today on the person's screen; 'as_it_grows' = what it means with more screens, people, platforms or content. One plain sentence each, 25 words at most. Lines restate the question's own option text, its Decision Cards (research/L*.md, benchmarks/L09) and the house standards; a line that is OpenDesigner's own reasoning ends with ' [inferred]'. evidence: Decision Card ids (DC-...) and learning-wiki source ids (S-L19-..., learn/sids.json) the lines rest on; standards: house standards (synthesis/standards.json) a line must respect or cites, so no line contradicts them. Keys match questionnaire.json option values. tools/build_data.py copies the lines into questions.json (now, grows) and the stage files ('Now: ... As it grows: ...'). The policy that uses them: learn/wiki/synthesis/decide-or-ask.md.

product-app.now: Parts are built for your app alone, so the look can stay tight and specific. [inferred]
product-app.as_it_grows: Adding a marketing site or emails later means making parts more general and adding token layers.

marketing.now: Adds a louder, expressive layer for the marketing site next to the calm app layer, as Carbon does.
marketing.as_it_grows: Marketing and app styles tend to drift apart, so someone must keep the shared colors and type in step.

internal-tools.now: In-house tools are usually dense: smaller text and tighter rows so more fits on screen. [inferred]
internal-tools.as_it_grows: Each new tool reuses the same parts; dense screens get a compact mode instead of a second system.

docs-content.now: Long reading pages add rules for comfortable line length and paragraph spacing. [inferred]
docs-content.as_it_grows: If articles pass about a third of your pages, a second, bigger set of heading styles pays off.

email.now: Email can show only simple styling, so the system must also write its colors and text out for email.
email.as_it_grows: Every new email template reuses those outputs; anything email cannot show needs a plain fallback. [inferred]

partner-embed.now: Parts must work inside other people's sites, so they get general names like 'card', not 'product card'.
partner-embed.as_it_grows: Partners build on your parts, so changes need public docs and stricter version numbers.

engineers.now: Adds component docs and code packages that engineers can install.
engineers.as_it_grows: More engineers and projects mean more packages to version and keep in step. [inferred]

designers.now: Adds a design-tool library, such as Figma, that mirrors the tokens.
designers.as_it_grows: Without automatic sync, the design library and the code drift apart, a common team complaint.

content-pm.now: Adds usage and voice guidance, so writers know how the product talks.
content-pm.as_it_grows: As more people write copy, the shared voice traits settle arguments and keep screens sounding alike.

partners.now: Adds public docs and stricter version numbers, because outside teams build on the system.
partners.as_it_grows: Every breaking change then affects people outside your team, so changes slow down and need notice. [inferred]

ai-agents.now: Adds files AI coding tools can read, such as DESIGN.md, so they follow the system.
ai-agents.as_it_grows: Every screen an AI writes later reads the same written rules, so it needs less re-explaining. [inferred]

dense.now: Body text 13-14 px and controls 28-32 px, so more rows fit; it looks professional and packed.
dense.as_it_grows: Fits data tools as they grow, but touch and occasional use need a roomier mode; tap targets never shrink.

regular.now: Body text 16 px and controls 36-40 px: balanced for an everyday app.
regular.as_it_grows: The safe middle: data-heavy pages can add a compact mode later instead of a second system.

large.now: Body text 17 px or more and 44-48 px targets: calm and easy to read and tap on phones.
large.as_it_grows: Suits public and phone use; dense admin screens added later would need a compact mode. [inferred]

A playful-serious.now: Toward playful: strong color, big round corners, springier motion. Toward serious: neutral colors, small corners, calm motion.
A playful-serious.as_it_grows: Every new screen inherits this mood; Google's research warns that expressive styles may not suit banking.

B friendly-authoritative.now: Toward friendly: warm grays, rounded corners, casual wording. Toward authoritative: cool grays or black, tighter corners, strong lines.
B friendly-authoritative.as_it_grows: It also sets how the words sound, so new copy, errors and help text follow the same tone.

C minimal-rich.now: Toward minimal: near gray, one accent, lots of space. Toward rich: several colors, visible boxes, filled icons, big moments.
C minimal-rich.as_it_grows: Minimal stays calm as screens multiply; rich needs rules for where extra color goes, or screens get busy. [inferred]

D calm-energetic.now: Toward calm: short, subtle motion, lighter weights, soft colors. Toward energetic: livelier motion, heavier weights, stronger colors.
D calm-energetic.as_it_grows: Even when energetic, lively motion stays on rare moments; things people do many times a day stay quiet.

E premium-everyday.now: Toward premium: taller, elegant type, restrained colors, subtle materials. Toward everyday: sturdy type, bright colors, flat fills.
E premium-everyday.as_it_grows: Premium depends on restraint, so each new feature must resist adding color; everyday tolerates more variety. [inferred]

F modern-heritage.now: Toward modern: geometric fonts, generated color shades, a code font. Toward heritage: serif fonts, hand-picked fixed colors.
F modern-heritage.as_it_grows: Generated shades extend to new colors on their own; a hand-picked palette needs a person for every new shade. [inferred]

G bold-deferential.now: Toward bold: brand color on big areas, custom parts everywhere. Toward deferential: accent on key actions only, native fonts and controls.
G bold-deferential.as_it_grows: Bold means rebuilding custom parts for every platform and OS update; deferential gets platform updates for free.

productive.now: Calm and efficient everywhere, with no big animated moments, like Carbon's product screens.
productive.as_it_grows: Stays comfortable for daily use as features pile up; a strong minority prefers calm, though it can seem less modern.

hero-moments.now: Calm everywhere, plus one or two big moments, such as a first success, with bolder type and motion.
hero-moments.as_it_grows: Big moments stay rare, like first run or finishing a task; everyday actions stay quiet, per house standards.

expressive.now: Lively throughout: varied shapes, rich color, bigger type and fluid motion; Google's tests found it feels more modern.
expressive.as_it_grows: Overdone, it hurts ease of use; house standards still keep motion off things people do many times a day.

two-sets.now: A calm product text scale plus a separate, dramatic set with huge headings for marketing and articles.
two-sets.as_it_grows: Pays off once over a third of pages are marketing or editorial; two sets to keep in step across screen sizes.

emphasized.now: One scale, plus heavier versions of styles for actions and headlines, like Material 3 Expressive.
emphasized.as_it_grows: One scale to maintain; emphasis grows by weight rather than new sizes, so pages stay consistent. [inferred]

brand-face.now: One scale, with your brand font kept for special brand moments, like Atlassian's Charlie Sans.
brand-face.as_it_grows: Brand moments stay recognizable as you grow, but the extra font must be licensed and loaded everywhere. [inferred]

productive-only.now: One product scale only, like Polaris and Primer: calm, with small jumps between sizes.
productive-only.as_it_grows: Simplest to keep; if a marketing site arrives, it will likely need 3-4 bigger display styles added.

web.now: One set of CSS files, and your brand can show in every pixel.
web.as_it_grows: Adding apps later brings each platform's own habits, units and screen readers to design and test for.

ios.now: Apple styles the bars, controls and sheets (Liquid Glass); sizes are in points, and text follows Dynamic Type.
ios.as_it_grows: Apple's redesigns reach standard parts for free; parts you custom-build must be updated by hand.

android.now: Material 3 habits and dp units; layouts for large screens (600 dp and up) are required.
android.as_it_grows: Tablets and foldables come with it, so wider layouts with panes are needed from day one.

desktop.now: A desktop app; built with web tech, it must respect the native window frame or it feels like a website. [inferred]
desktop.as_it_grows: Windows resize freely, so layouts must change by window size, never by device type.

secondary.now: Watch, TV, car or headset: only colors, text roles and icons carry over, inside platform templates.
secondary.as_it_grows: Each device adds its own text sizes and focus styles; the smaller or farther the screen, the less custom UI survives. [inferred]

native-first.now: Uses the platform's own controls almost everywhere; your brand shows in content, accents, images and words.
native-first.as_it_grows: OS updates and accessibility come built in, but the app looks more like other apps on the device.

hybrid.now: Brand colors, type and signature moments, with native navigation, back gestures, sheets and pickers.
hybrid.as_it_grows: Share what people see as the brand, keep how the phone works native: about 80% native, 20% signature.

brand-first.now: The same custom look on every platform; it can feel foreign, with the wrong back gestures or sheets.
brand-first.as_it_grows: Every OS change must be rebuilt by hand, and screen reader and text-size support must be rebuilt too.

principles.now: Platforms share only ideas, so each app can look quite different.
principles.as_it_grows: Easiest to start, but the apps drift apart as teams grow, because nothing concrete is shared. [inferred]

tokens.now: Same colors, type personality and spacing everywhere, with components built to fit each platform.
tokens.as_it_grows: Share the what (names and decisions) everywhere and let each platform's code do the how, so it still feels native. [inferred]

specs.now: One plan per component (parts, states, screen reader notes), coded separately per platform, like Uber Base.
specs.as_it_grows: One plan can serve many code stacks, but every plan change must then be built once per platform. [inferred]

code.now: Identical component code on every platform, so everything looks the same.
code.as_it_grows: Features ship everywhere at once, but the app feels least native, and one bug reaches every platform. [inferred]

phone.now: Phones get layouts designed for them, because core tasks happen there.
phone.as_it_grows: Devices that only adapt the phone layout look stretched, which Google now penalizes on large screens.

tablet-foldable.now: Adds rails, sidebars and two or three panes; Android ignores orientation locks at 600 dp and up.
tablet-foldable.as_it_grows: Android forces this size on apps anyway, so skipping it means a stretched phone layout there.

desktop-web.now: Wide layouts for desktop and web are designed properly, not stretched from the phone.
desktop-web.as_it_grows: Big screens add panes and sidebars that change the product's shape; iPad windows make any size normal.

watch.now: A dark, glanceable version with scrolling lists; only colors, type and icons travel.
watch.as_it_grows: Adds its own watch text sizes and motion values to maintain alongside the main system.

tv.now: Big type, focus rows you move through with a remote, 66 pt targets and a safe border.
tv.as_it_grows: Adds a TV text scale and focus styles to every component that appears there.

car.now: Uses the car system's templates: large, sparse, high-contrast screens with little room for your brand.
car.as_it_grows: Templates limit custom UI, so only colors, type and icons carry over from the main system.

spatial.now: Glass windows floating at a distance, with 60 pt targets.
spatial.as_it_grows: Adds comfort rules, such as no motion at the edge of vision, to every animated part.

builder.now: OpenDesigner's files are the master copy; one step writes tokens, CSS, native code and design-tool files.
builder.as_it_grows: Design tools stay mirrors refreshed from one master; 60% of teams have no such token automation.

token-file.now: A token file in git is the master; code and Figma are fed from it.
token-file.as_it_grows: Best once two or more code platforms exist, and it keeps colors Figma cannot hold, like OKLCH. [inferred]

code.now: Tokens and components live in code, and design tools copy from it, as most practitioners now work.
code.as_it_grows: Real components can be tested automatically, but visual exploration becomes a second-class copy.

design-file.now: Figma variables are the master, and designers own the tokens.
design-file.as_it_grows: Fits one web platform; Figma drops some color formats, so with more platforms the master should move to files. [inferred]

flat2.now: Mostly flat surfaces, subtle shadows or tone steps, and clear signs of what to click: neutral and efficient.
flat2.as_it_grows: A durable base that ages well as screens pile up; keep neo-brutalist and maximal styles for marketing pages.

tonal.now: Surfaces separate by soft color steps: friendly and systematic, like Material 3.
tonal.as_it_grows: Needs 4-5 close gray steps and matches Android's own look as you add platforms. [inferred]

glass.now: See-through bars and controls over the content: premium and native on Apple, but it can hide content.
glass.as_it_grows: Every glass surface needs a solid version for people who reduce transparency or raise contrast; large blurs may also slow drawing. [inferred]

neo-brutalist.now: Thick borders, hard offset shadows and 2-3 bold colors: loud, indie and memorable.
neo-brutalist.as_it_grows: Its solid borders go against a house standard, and research keeps it to marketing or indie products.

soft.now: Raised same-color surfaces with soft paired shadows: tactile but vague, and edges often fail contrast.
soft.as_it_grows: Every clickable part needs added borders to reach 3:1 contrast, which undoes much of the look. [inferred]

maximal.now: Vibrant colors, overlapping visuals and bold type: energetic but busy.
maximal.as_it_grows: Meant for marketing only; inside the app, the busyness grows with every screen. [inferred]

compact.now: More data per screen with tighter rows: looks efficient and expert.
compact.as_it_grows: Needs strong grouping and clear signs of what to click as screens fill; tap targets keep their minimum size.

comfortable.now: Calmer and touch-friendly, with room around each item.
comfortable.as_it_grows: A good base for app screens; data-heavy tables and lists can add a compact mode later.

spacious.now: Lots of space: calm, premium and focused on one message.
spacious.as_it_grows: Great for marketing and focused tasks, but it slows down people who come back often.

user-selectable.now: A default density plus a compact mode people can switch on, like Atlassian and Salesforce.
user-selectable.as_it_grows: Only data-heavy parts (tables, lists, menus, trees) need both sizes; targets never shrink in either mode.

keep-hex.now: Your exact brand colors stay, and a person tunes each shade by hand.
keep-hex.as_it_grows: Keeps the brand's nuance, but every new color, mode or theme needs hand-tuning again. [inferred]

seed.now: One color generates even, matching shades for everything, like Material and Ant.
seed.as_it_grows: New colors and dark mode come out consistent; still check contrast, since Ant's own default blue fails with white text.

seed-3.now: Three inputs (brand color, gray base and contrast) generate the whole palette.
seed-3.as_it_grows: Easy to retheme later: Linear replaced 98 per-theme variables with these three.

contrast-targets.now: Each shade is set by a contrast goal, so text on every color stays readable.
contrast-targets.as_it_grows: Readability stays predictable across every new color and theme you add.

accent.now: Brand color only on main buttons, links, status and the selected tab: calm and content-first.
accent.as_it_grows: Stays calm as screens multiply and suits Apple's glass look; each view gives the color to one key element.

signature-surface.now: One standout area, like Slack's purple sidebar, carries the brand: instantly recognizable.
signature-surface.as_it_grows: Every new layout must keep room for that area, or the recognition fades. [inferred]

flooded-chrome.now: Brand color on the app bars and floating buttons: louder and more playful.
flooded-chrome.as_it_grows: Normal on Android, but on iOS 26 a tinted bar reads as dated and 'fighting the glass'. [inferred]

content-layer.now: Brand color lives in the content, which scrolls under clear glass controls: modern, Apple 2026 style.
content-layer.as_it_grows: Each new screen needs colorful content to show the brand, and glass over bright content needs dimming for contrast. [inferred]

neutral-first.now: Mostly gray, with a faint brand tint on bars and menus, as Linear did with its blue.
neutral-first.as_it_grows: Very calm at any size; the brand then relies on logo, type and words more than color. [inferred]

monochrome.now: All gray or nearly gray: calm, premium and technical, like Polaris's black brand.
monochrome.as_it_grows: Status colors stand out clearly because little else is colorful; charts still need their own colors. [inferred]

tonal.now: Low to medium color: friendly and balanced, Material's default.
tonal.as_it_grows: The safe default for work products: keep big surfaces soft and spend strong color on small, meaningful parts.

vivid.now: Strong, saturated colors: energetic and consumer-grade.
vivid.as_it_grows: As screens fill, everything shouts and status colors lose punch, so status also needs icons or words. [inferred]

expressive.now: Colors turned away from your brand hue: surprising and playful, like Material Expressive.
expressive.as_it_grows: Your exact brand hue may barely appear, so recognition must come from other parts. [inferred]

fidelity.now: Your brand hue stays exact in containers and fills.
fidelity.as_it_grows: Best when the hue is a legal or recognition asset; light brand colors will need dark text on buttons.

static.now: Your brand colors stay fixed on every device; best for work apps and iOS.
static.as_it_grows: Screenshots and brand recall stay the same for everyone as the product spreads. [inferred]

dynamic-optional.now: Fixed brand colors by default; Android users can switch on colors from their wallpaper.
dynamic-optional.as_it_grows: Brand and error colors stay fixed, but testing grows: each wallpaper and mode can change the colors.

follow-os.now: Colors follow the wallpaper or device accent: personal and native.
follow-os.as_it_grows: Every user's screenshots differ and brand recall weakens; keep brand-critical and status colors fixed. [inferred]

oklch.now: Shades built so each step looks equally heavy in every color: the modern web method.
oklch.as_it_grows: New colors slot in without shifting what looks important; contrast still gets checked after generation. [inferred]

hct.now: Material's method, numbered by tone, so the same tone gives the same brightness in every hue.
hct.as_it_grows: Needed if the system feeds Android dynamic color, and Material's tools read it on every platform.

contrast-indexed.now: Every step has the same contrast in every color, like Spectrum's 700 steps.
contrast-indexed.as_it_grows: Best if people can recolor the accent: every new accent passes the same text pairings.

hand-tuned.now: Each color is tuned by hand: more character, less predictable.
hand-tuned.as_it_grows: Swapping or adding a hue can make buttons suddenly lighter or darker, so each one needs checking. [inferred]

preset.now: A ready-made palette like Tailwind's or Radix's: fast, with a recognizable stock look.
preset.as_it_grows: Quick to extend, but your product shares its colors with many others. [inferred]

lab-hsl.now: Older methods: Lab was Stripe's 2019 fix, and HSL washes out yellows and muddies blues.
lab-hsl.as_it_grows: HSL shades stay uneven with every color you add, so it is best avoided.

container-tiers.now: Named layers from lowest to highest, not tied to shadows: flat, calm and modern, like Material 3.
container-tiers.as_it_grows: Works without shadows in both modes; clickable layers still need visible edges. [inferred]

alternating.now: Layers alternate shades in light mode and step lighter in dark: crisp and grid-like, like Carbon.
alternating.as_it_grows: Clear on dense enterprise screens; deep nesting needs care so layers don't blur together. [inferred]

elevation-named.now: Layers named by height, like Atlassian's raised and overlay levels.
elevation-named.as_it_grows: Names tie color to shadow height, so changing the depth style later touches both. [inferred]

role-tiers.now: 4-5 layers named by job (base, raised, overlay, sunken), each with its own light and dark color.
role-tiers.as_it_grows: New parts pick a layer by its job, and dark mode shows depth with lighter surfaces, not glowing shadows.

tone-reassign.now: Same color families, with each job moved to a new shade in dark mode, like Material.
tone-reassign.as_it_grows: What looks most important stays the same in both modes as screens are added.

mirrored.now: A mirrored ramp (700 in light is 400 in dark) with separate dark grays, like Atlassian.
mirrored.as_it_grows: Each new color gets its dark version by role, and every pair is re-checked for contrast.

separate.now: Separate hand-tuned dark scales, like Radix and Primer: richer darks.
separate.as_it_grows: Looks richer but drifts over time: every new color needs its own dark scale tuned. [inferred]

aa.now: Text needs 4.5:1 contrast, large text and parts 3:1, which allows softer gray text and lighter tints.
aa.as_it_grows: Every new color pair is tested against it in every mode, at every build.

aaa.now: Text needs 7:1 contrast: darker gray text and deeper accents, which feels heavier and starker. [inferred]
aaa.as_it_grows: Primer and Material keep it for high-contrast modes; applied everywhere, it limits every new color choice. [inferred]

aa-apca.now: AA must pass, plus APCA advice on body text, as Radix and Geist do.
aa-apca.as_it_grows: Keeps you at AA today and closer to WCAG 3, which is still a draft. [inferred]

system.now: Each device's own font, such as SF Pro or Roboto: native and invisible, so content leads.
system.as_it_grows: Nothing to load or license, and native text-size settings work for free; the brand must show elsewhere.

open-neutral.now: A free, plain font like Inter: the neutral SaaS look.
open-neutral.as_it_grows: Looks the same on every platform with no license cost, but many products share it. [inferred]

open-custom.now: A free font with character, like IBM Plex or Geist: recognizable without license fees.
open-custom.as_it_grows: Consistent across platforms; native apps must bundle it and support text-size settings themselves. [inferred]

brand-display.now: Your brand font for headlines and the system font for body text, as Apple advises.
brand-display.as_it_grows: Headlines stay recognizable while small text stays legible on every new platform.

brand-everywhere.now: Your own font everywhere, like Uber Move or Airbnb Cereal: the strongest identity.
brand-everywhere.as_it_grows: Every platform must bundle it and rebuild text scaling; keep it out of body text if it looks weak at 13 pt.

static.now: Fixed weights only, such as regular and bold: simplest, and works with any font.
static.as_it_grows: Big headings need tighter letter spacing and line heights set by hand, since letters don't reshape by size.

variable-wght.now: In-between weights, like Polaris's 450 and 550, for finer steps of emphasis.
variable-wght.as_it_grows: New text styles can use finer emphasis steps without adding font files. [inferred]

variable-opsz.now: Weights plus letter shapes that adjust to size: sturdier small text and sleeker headings.
variable-opsz.as_it_grows: Every new size looks right on its own where the font supports it; otherwise heading spacing is set by hand.

4-grid-8-rhythm.now: Spacing named in steps of 8, with 2, 4 and 6 kept for small gaps inside components.
4-grid-8-rhythm.as_it_grows: What Material 3, Atlassian and Spectrum ship; 24, 44 and 48 px targets build from whole steps.

4.now: Steps of 4 everywhere: finer control and a more compact, tool-like feel.
4.as_it_grows: Suits dense, data-heavy tools; with many close steps, people may pick gaps that look almost the same. [inferred]

8.now: Steps of 8 with few in-between: chunky, calm and clearly different gaps.
8.as_it_grows: Rhythm stays obvious on marketing and content pages; tight spots like icon labels may need exceptions. [inferred]

rem-16.now: Spacing in rem units based on 16 px, like Bootstrap, so it follows the person's text-size setting on the web.
rem-16.as_it_grows: Spacing grows when people enlarge text; native apps convert it to their own point and dp units. [inferred]

hybrid.now: Small steps at the bottom and bigger jumps at the top: tight inside groups, loose between them.
hybrid.as_it_grows: About 12-15 steps cover app and marketing pages, with the big top steps kept for page sections.

linear.now: Even 4 px steps: many choices close together.
linear.as_it_grows: Near-identical gaps like 20, 24 and 28 creep in and read as inconsistency.

geometric.now: Each step doubles (2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64): very clear levels.
geometric.as_it_grows: Grouping reads instantly, but big jumps may leave no good size for some layouts. [inferred]

material.now: Layouts change at 600, 840, 1200 and 1600: works for Android and the web.
material.as_it_grows: One set shared across platforms; Material notes some products never need the largest sizes.

tailwind.now: Layouts change at 640, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1536: the common web-only set.
tailwind.as_it_grows: Fine while you stay on the web; adding native apps later means mapping to their own size classes. [inferred]

bootstrap.now: Layouts change at 576, 768, 992, 1200 and 1400: Bootstrap's set.
bootstrap.as_it_grows: Familiar to Bootstrap teams; more breakpoints mean smoother changes but more design and testing. [inferred]

apple-size-classes.now: The system reports compact or regular width and height, and the layout follows that.
apple-size-classes.as_it_grows: Handles any iPad window size, because layout follows window size, never device type.

square.now: Corners of 0-2 px: official and engineered, like GOV.UK and Carbon.
square.as_it_grows: Sharp corners become a deliberate brand choice, since even Carbon is adding roundness; iOS rounds its own controls anyway. [inferred]

subtle.now: Corners of 4-6 px: businesslike, like Primer and Atlassian.
subtle.as_it_grows: The safest default across audiences; containers get 8-12 px, and focus rings follow the corners.

soft.now: Corners of 8-12 px: friendly and modern, like Polaris and Airbnb.
soft.as_it_grows: Nested cards need matching inner corners, which iOS expects and the web must work out itself. [inferred]

pill.now: Fully round ends: consumer, playful and touch-first, like Material 3 and iOS 26.
pill.as_it_grows: Needs taller controls, so it fits poorly on dense, short controls in data tools.

rule-based.now: Corners set by size, like Spectrum's 6-10 px, or matched to the container, as Apple does.
rule-based.as_it_grows: New parts get the right corner from their size or container, without a new decision. [inferred]

shadow.now: A ladder of shadows: tactile and clearly layered, like Fluent and Polaris.
shadow.as_it_grows: Best kept for things that float, like menus and dialogs; static cards can use color steps instead.

tonal.now: Layers separate by color steps: flat, calm and color-forward, like Carbon and Linear.
tonal.as_it_grows: Suits data-dense tools; needs 4-5 close gray steps, and clickable card edges need 3:1 contrast.

borders.now: Thin lines only: dense and technical, like GOV.UK and Primer.
borders.as_it_grows: A house standard prefers see-through shadows to solid borders, and clickable card edges need 3:1 contrast.

ring-shadow.now: A faint 1 px ring plus a soft shadow: crisp edges, like Radix, Geist and Airbnb.
ring-shadow.as_it_grows: Matches the house standard's see-through edges; in dark mode, lighter surfaces replace shadows.

glass.now: Frosted, see-through materials: premium and content-first, like Apple's Liquid Glass.
glass.as_it_grows: Every glass surface needs a solid version for people who reduce transparency or raise contrast; large blurs may also slow drawing. [inferred]

none.now: Almost nothing moves; press feedback and quick fades that explain a change stay. Still and calm, like GOV.UK.
none.as_it_grows: Stays consistent as screens grow, but rare moments like a first success get no extra life. [inferred]

productive.now: Quick, plain movements with no bounce: fast and competent.
productive.as_it_grows: Fits frequent actions as features grow; things done 100+ times a day still get no animation at all.

two-mode.now: Quick, plain motion for most actions, with bolder motion kept for a few key moments.
two-mode.as_it_grows: Bold moments stay rare, like onboarding or a first success; daily actions stay quick and quiet, and core navigation doesn't animate.

springs.now: Movement feels physical and can be caught mid-way; bounce stays for flicks, drags and rare playful moments, per house standards.
springs.as_it_grows: Springs drive whatever a finger moves; motion nobody touched keeps plain timing curves, and the web needs a JavaScript spring library.

upload.now: Your existing guide becomes the rules for all product words.
upload.as_it_grows: Every new screen, error and empty state follows it, and copy arguments settle by pointing to it.

plainspoken.now: Plainspoken and genuine, with dry humor, like Mailchimp.
plainspoken.as_it_grows: Voice stays the same everywhere while tone softens for errors and serious moments, so humor gets rationed. [inferred]

warm-crisp.now: Warm and relaxed, crisp and clear, ready to help, like Microsoft.
warm-crisp.as_it_grows: Holds up as more writers join, as long as each trait has a 'but not' so it isn't vague. [inferred]

bold-optimistic.now: Bold, optimistic and practical with a wink, like Atlassian.
bold-optimistic.as_it_grows: Optimism must not hide bad news, so error and billing messages need a plainer tone. [inferred]

custom.now: Your own 3-4 traits in 'X, but not Y' form, with words to avoid.
custom.as_it_grows: Example lines per trait let new writers and AI tools match it; a content designer should review it. [inferred]
